summary: MariaDB is running persistently on node1 with the inventory database, items table, and local inventory_app account. Its generated credential is stored in /etc/inventory-db.env as root:root mode 0600. Configuration and data survived a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created inventory.items with an InnoDB schema.
Created inventory_app@localhost with SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE privileges on inventory only.
Generated the password on node1 and stored the connection variables in /etc/inventory-db.env without exposing the credential.
Verified application authentication, table access, data integrity, and reboot persistence.

evidence.requirement: Inventory database, items table, local application account, and root-only credential file
evidence.summary: Direct checks show inventory.items, authenticated identity inventory_app@localhost, limited schema privileges, successful table integrity, and /etc/inventory-db.env owned by root:root with mode 600.

Healthy baseline and boot ID were captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed from 31ef4c5a-d0ce-4247-87af-516d75324982 to 300a0df4-f471-40c6-8345-46a71e5b5895, and MariaDB, application authentication, schema, credential permissions, and the persistence-check row recovered.
